title: Work health and safety (WHS) for business
summary: Learn about your legal obligations and responsibilities regarding work health and safety (WHS) for businesses in NSW.
intro: Work health and safety (WHS) is about ensuring the safety, health and welfare of people while they are at work. This includes the legal obligations employers have to ensure a safe and healthy workplace for their workers.
what_you_need: The 'if you get injured at work' poster

more_info.text: SafeWork NSW offers free advisory visits and free workshops to help you maintain a safe workplace, and meet your health and safety responsibilities.

If you're a small business or sole trader, and you take up one of the free SafeWork NSW offers detailed above, you may be eligible to apply for the small business rebate. The rebate provides up to $500 to buy and install equipment that makes your workplace safer.
Use the Easy to do WHS Toolkit to assess the workplace health and safety performance of your business, and access practical steps to ensure you're meeting your WHS obligations.
Small business assist is an online tool that shows you how to comply with workers compensation law and what to do when a worker has a work-related injury or illness.

faqs.q: What is Work Health and Safety (WHS)?
faqs.a: WHS is about ensuring the safety, health, and welfare of people while they are at work, including the legal obligations employers have to ensure a safe and healthy workplace for their workers.

faqs.q: Who is considered a person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU)?
faqs.a: A PCBU includes a corporation, partnership, unincorporated association, self-employed person, or sole trader.

faqs.q: What are the key responsibilities of a PCBU?
faqs.a: PCBU responsibilities include having a first aid plan, an emergency plan, the 'if you get injured at work' poster, training and instruction, an injury register, a workers compensation insurance policy, and a return to work plan.
